paper.title: Bounded Recursive Self-Improvement
paper.central_claim: AERA (autocatalytic, endogenous, reflective architecture) lets a seed-based system learn and revise its own executable models from experience under bounded resources, yielding bounded recursive self-improvement; a prototype (S1) learns real-time multimodal interview skills by observing humans with no errors afterwards.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by design (no probing).

rationale: Detailed reliability-gated executable-model learning architecture with a single author-judged demonstration; no baselines, ablations, held-out scenarios, cost, or recursive-level experiment. Task-level, scoped.

evidence.quote: Based on principles of autocatalysis, endogeny, and reflectivity, the work provides an architectural blueprint for constructing systems with high levels of operational autonomy in underspecified circumstances
evidence.support_explanation: Claim: AERA is a seed-based architecture whose own executable knowledge is learned and rewritten by its operation.

evidence.quote: A prototype system has been implemented and demonstrated to learn a complex real-world task
evidence.support_explanation: The only empirical evidence is one prototype (S1) on multimodal dialogue by observation.

evidence.quote: Current engineering methodologies assume that code is written by humans.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: hand-written knowledge bases do not scale to autonomous systems.

evidence.quote: Model acquisition is triggered by either the unpredicted success of a goal or the failure of a prediction.
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate generation rule: surprise (unpredicted success or failed prediction) triggers model extraction.

evidence.quote: Under our assumption of insufficient knowledge, explaining in this case is much closer to guessing than to proving
evidence.support_explanation: New models are heuristic guesses based on temporal precedence; acceptance is by later performance.

evidence.quote: new code (models) is given an initial reliability that is very likely to be lower than that of established code
evidence.support_explanation: Admission rule: new models start with low reliability and only gain influence after positive evidence.

evidence.quote: If the reliability of a model drops below a threshold THR1 then it is phased out
evidence.support_explanation: Retirement gate: phase-out at THR1, deletion at THR2; reversible while phased out.

evidence.quote: the model is deleted as are all the programs that were created to manage its productions
evidence.support_explanation: Deletion below THR2 removes the model and dependent programs; LRU garbage collector also described.

evidence.quote: Even though self-modeling for meta-control has not been leveraged in our S1 demonstrator, this functionality has been implemented and is operational.
evidence.support_explanation: The recursive meta-level (self-modeling, self-compilation) is not part of the reported experiments.

evidence.quote: Our results are analyzed using t-patterns
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation relies on t-pattern analysis of recorded interaction, a descriptive temporal-pattern method.

evidence.quote: In E1 S1 only has to observe the human interaction for about 2.5 minutes before it is able to predict accurately their behavior
evidence.support_explanation: E1 data volume: about 2.5 min observation, about 17 turns, 0 errors (Table 4).

evidence.quote: In E2 the observation period was 20 hours, which is dramatically higher than that required in E1 for an equivalent error-free performance.
evidence.support_explanation: E2 observation about 20 h, about 8000 turns observed, 0 errors (Table 10).

evidence.quote: A thorough inspection of the videos of S1 revealed no errors in the interaction on behalf of S1
evidence.support_explanation: Error-free judgement is by inspection of videos; no defined error criterion or independent rater.

evidence.quote: recordings of S1 interacting in either role with one of the humans (same as who participated in the human-human scenario)
evidence.support_explanation: Test interaction reuses a participant from the observation phase; same scenario and developers as participants.

evidence.quote: Due to the number of commission errors in the speech recognizer its output was restricted to the set of 100 permissible words
evidence.support_explanation: Input channel was filtered to a 100-word vocabulary in E2.

evidence.quote: it consists of a set of primitive commands (move hand, grab, release, point at) and a set of dimensions for the input space
evidence.support_explanation: Seed content is hand-designed (primitives, drives, top-level models).

evidence.quote: in its current incarnation AERA is entirely dependent on observation, as learning is exclusively triggered by unexpected goal achievement, or a prediction that turns out to be wrong
evidence.support_explanation: Stated limitation of the learning trigger.

evidence.quote: To support the claim of achieving bounded self-improvement in general, one has to demonstrate a fundamental property namely, scalability.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede the scalability/bounded self-improvement claim is not yet supported.

evidence.quote: The Gödel Machine (GM) is a proposal to a general approach for imparting any system with recursive self-improvement and, as AIXI, remains to be implemented.
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage statement: GM/AIXI are unimplemented; AERA replaces proofs with experience-sanctioned improvement.

evidence.quote: In E2 S1 was given no grammar.
evidence.support_explanation: E2 provides no grammar, but the seed and drives are hand-crafted.

signatures.object: models (executable cause-effect programs) and composite states in AERA memory
signatures.information: sensory and internal inputs (instantiated models, success/failure facts), drives from seed, no external labels
signatures.operation: targeted pattern extractors build models from unexpected goal success or failed prediction; prediction/goal monitors update reliability
signatures.output: new models with low initial reliability; abstractions with variables; pre/post-condition models
signatures.conditions: time precedence heuristic; linear guards; learning priority tied to success-rate derivative
signatures.feedback: prediction/goal outcome evidence from the environment
signatures.selection_rule: reliability e+/(e+1); phase out below THR1, delete below THR2; LRU garbage collector
signatures.persistence: models held in memory and used by the executive
signatures.later_use: forward/backward chaining jobs scheduled by value-driven priorities
signatures.claimed_effect: error-free multimodal dialogue in either role after observation
signatures.failure_boundary: observation-only trigger; hidden causes; scalability untested; recursion not demonstrated

signatures.operation: meta-system adjusts thresholds, GC and drive priorities under congestion; self-compilation proposed
signatures.conditions: implemented but not used in S1
signatures.claimed_effect: graceful degradation under scarce resources (no results)

gap.author_gap: Engineered controllers cannot operate in partially known environments, re-define missions, handle complexity or degrade gracefully; hand-written code cannot scale; the Godel machine needs intractable proof search.
gap.checked_gap: Fixed object: hand-authored knowledge/control code; AERA lets the system add/remove small executable models itself. The recursion-specific gap (improver improving itself) is claimed but not exercised in S1.
gap.lineage: Godel machine/AIXI (theory), Schmidhuber self-modifying policies, SOAR/LIDA cognitive architectures, NARS -> AERA.
gap.closest_adjacent: Godel machine, AIXI, SOAR, LIDA, NARS (Wang), Schmidhuber et al. 1997.
gap.residue: How to realize practical self-modification that is bounded by resources and sanctioned by experience, not proofs.
gap.method_response: Fine-grained executable models, reliability-gated additions/removals, value-driven scheduling, operational reflectivity.
gap.remaining_gap: Curiosity, hidden causation, scalability, demonstration of meta-level self-improvement.
unresolved: no later-work comparison; neighbors are as cited in the report

matches.tactic_steps_checked: One uniform term/model scheme for speech, gesture and internal traces processed by the same executive; the C18 tokenizer/serializer tactic is not used, so no sub-card.
matches.reason: Uniform fine-grained executable knowledge is a design principle that is a separate operation from surprise-driven model learning.

rs_pattern.resolves_problem: no for recursive self-improvement/bounded scaling; narrow yes for learning two interview tasks per author inspection.

claims.text: S1 learns interviewer and interviewee roles by observation and then performs error-free

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A hand-seeded AERA prototype learned executable models that let it conduct two scripted-like multimodal interviews error-free by author inspection; the recursion, boundedness and scalability claims are not tested.

G.reason: Concrete lineage (Godel machine/AIXI intractability, SOAR/LIDA lack of operational reflectivity, NARS closest) with a stated residual and an explicit list of what remains (curiosity, hidden causation, scalability); the opening gap in terms of four AGI-level features is broad.

M.reason: Surprise-triggered model acquisition, reliability-gated admission/retirement and abstraction form a complete learning mechanism with equations; the link from this to recursive self-improvement rests on an unexercised meta-level, and the temporal-precedence-as-causality heuristic is a weak assumption.

X.reason: Equations, program types, thresholds and the model life cycle are described and boundaries/limitations are stated; many parameter values, seed definitions and Replicode code are deferred to other reports, and the meta-control path is not exercised.

E.measurement.reason: Success is judged by inspection of videos with no operational error definition or independent rater, and t-pattern analysis describes behavioral similarity rather than correctness; no trivial baseline.

E.causality.reason: No baselines, ablations or controls; attribution relies only on the fact that the seed lacks the learned behavior, and E2 uses a 100-word filtered channel and hand-built seed.

E.holdout.reason: Testing is a later session of the same scenario with a participant from the observation phase and developers as participants; there are no held-out scenarios or tasks.

E.statistics.reason: Observation durations and turn counts are given and t-pattern significance thresholds are reported, but there is one prototype, one run per experiment and no test-turn denominator or uncertainty for the zero-error claim.

E.cost.reason: Only data cost is reported (2.5 min, 20 h of observation); the bounded-resource claim has no CPU, memory or latency measurements.
